categories.main_business_segments: QXO (formerly SilverSun Technologies) operates primarily through three business segments: (1) Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and accounting software resale and implementation, (2) value-added consulting and professional services (including custom programming, training, and technical support), and (3) IT managed services, including cybersecurity, application hosting, disaster recovery, and business continuity. The company also develops proprietary software enhancements and integrations for ERP systems.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: QXO leverages leading ERP platforms such as Sage (including Sage Intacct) and Acumatica, offering both on-premise and cloud-based solutions. The company employs a dual-shore software development approach, with U.S.-based technical leadership and offshore development teams, to build proprietary ERP enhancements and integrations. Its managed services utilize Microsoft-certified infrastructure and proprietary cybersecurity-as-a-service offerings, while its consulting and support services are delivered by certified professionals.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company primarily serves small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in the manufacturing, distribution, and professional services sectors. Its solutions are tailored to organizations seeking digital transformation, improved business management, and enhanced IT security, with a focus on industries requiring compliance and operational efficiency.
categories.geographic_coverage: QXO operates nationwide in the United States, with customer concentrations in the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area, Arizona, Connecticut, Southern California, North Carolina, Washington, Oregon, and Illinois. Through acquisitions, the company has expanded its presence to most U.S. states and also serves clients in Canada, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
categories.supply_chain_position: QXO acts as a value-added reseller (VAR) and independent software vendor (ISV), operating downstream in the supply chain by delivering, customizing, and supporting business management software and IT services directly to end customers. It also provides integration and support services for third-party software vendors.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategy emphasizes organic growth through recurring revenue, customer retention, and up-selling/cross-selling advanced technologies and add-ons. It actively pursues acquisitions to expand geographic reach, customer base, and technical capabilities. R&D efforts focus on developing ERP enhancements, integrations, and new managed services, with a strong emphasis on cloud migration, cybersecurity, and automation.
categories.revenue_model: QXO generates revenue through a mix of software product sales (both perpetual and subscription-based), professional and consulting services (billed as time and materials, prepaid, or annual contracts), managed IT services (recurring monthly or annual fees), and proprietary software licensing. A growing portion of revenue is recurring, driven by cloud subscriptions and managed services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes in a fragmented market against both large national firms and numerous small, local VARs and managed service providers. Major competitors include other Sage and Acumatica partners, as well as IT managed service providers. QXO positions itself as one of the largest Sage and Acumatica partners in North America, differentiating through deep technical expertise, proprietary integrations, and a combination of software and hardware capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2022, QXO reported revenues of $44.99 million, up 7.9% from the prior year. The company has a history of growth through both organic expansion and acquisitions, with a national customer base of approximately 8,000 active ERP clients. While it reported a net loss of $282,219 in 2022, the company maintains a strong liquidity position and continues to invest in growth initiatives.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: QXO’s value proposition centers on delivering tightly integrated, customizable business management solutions that enable SMBs to digitally transform operations, improve efficiency, and enhance security. Its unique strengths include proprietary ERP integrations, dual expertise in both software and hardware, a comprehensive managed services portfolio, and a consultative approach that fosters long-term customer relationships and high retention.
